top_entities.name: France
top_entities.news_summary: The 'Bloquons tout' ('Block Everything') movement mobilized nearly 200,000 people on 10 September 2026 to protest 2026 budget cuts to public services and the government's refusal of the proposed 'Zucman tax' on assets over EUR100M. The Ministry of Interior recorded 812 actions nationwide (550 gatherings, 262 blockades); more than 500 protesters were arrested. Security forces were accused of using excessive force during the 10 and 18 September demonstrations and of preventing journalists from covering the protests. Separately, France's UN mission in Geneva said on 13 September it 'regrets' a social-media post criticising the US over human rights, a dispute that has delayed the arrival of a new French ambassador to Washington.

top_entities.name: Slovenia
top_entities.news_summary: Thousands protested in Ljubljana on 9 September 2026 against Slovenia's opening of Israel's first embassy in the country, carrying Slovenian and Palestinian flags and criticizing PM Janez Jansa's diplomatic reversal from predecessor Robert Golob (who had called Israel's Gaza war a 'genocide'). The protest follows Slovenia's 26 August veto of a joint EU statement condemning Israeli West Bank settlement expansion, opposed by President Nataša Pirc Musar.

top_entities.name: Bolivia
top_entities.news_summary: Bolivia's currency crisis deepened: the boliviano lost as much as 76% of its value in the roughly three months since the government floated the exchange rate on 26 June 2026 (moving from a peg of 6.96/USD to as high as 9.73/USD). On 9 September the central bank injected US$35 million of its dwindling reserves into the market -- an emergency intervention described as necessary to 'mitigate unnecessary volatility' -- and separately began offering dollars directly to banks. This follows the state of emergency declared in June over anti-government protests tied to the economic crisis (24 deaths recorded by July).

top_entities.name: Brazil
top_entities.news_summary: An institutional crisis at Brazil's Supreme Court (STF) escalated after Justice Andre Mendonca lifted confidentiality on messages between Justice Alexandre de Moraes and banker Daniel Vorcaro (1 September). On 8 September Mendonca ordered preventive removal of Federal Police Director-General Andrei Rodrigues; on 9 September Justice Flavio Dino ordered his immediate reinstatement. The Court cancelled sessions on consecutive days amid allegations of graft, political bias and police interference among sitting justices, with the turmoil spilling into the October general election and right-wing candidate Flavio Bolsonaro reportedly overtaking President Lula in one poll (8 September).

top_entities.name: Syria
top_entities.news_summary: Syria is experiencing its most widespread protests since the fall of Bashar al-Assad, sparked by a 40% government-imposed hike in diesel prices (to 175 Syrian pounds/liter) on 14 September 2026. Demonstrators burned tires and blocked roads including the Damascus-Aleppo highway; unrest was reported in Aleppo, Dara'a, Deir Ezzor and Hasakah, with additional unrest in Kobani tied to the killing of a Kurdish citizen. UNDP estimates roughly 90% of Syrians live below the poverty line.

top_entities.name: Nepal
top_entities.news_summary: The Nepal-Tibet border flash-flood/glacier-collapse disaster (Langtang Lirung, originating 26 Aug 2026) death toll reached 1,386 in Nepal per NDRRMA's 12 September update (up from 1,356 on 7 September), with 6,827 injured and 5,130 still missing -- superseding the 1,114 figure carried from the prior cycle and the 1,050 figure reported 1 September. Reporting (CNN, ABC, Al Jazeera) continues to document that no glacier-hazard early-warning system existed for the affected area and that Nepal's SMS alert system failed or arrived late, repeating an unaddressed recommendation from a similar 2021 disaster. Most of the roughly 900 bodies recovered by 1 September remained unidentified.

top_entities.name: Cabo Verde
top_entities.news_summary: A passenger bus carrying secondary-school students on a field trip plunged roughly 30 metres into a ravine on Fogo Island on the night of 5 September 2026, killing at least 25 (mostly children and teenagers) and injuring 14 -- the deadliest road accident in Cape Verde's history. The government declared two days of national mourning and set up a crisis office. Separately, surging fuel prices (reported 6 September) are straining the fishing and transport sectors nationally.

top_entities.name: Cape Verde
top_entities.news_summary: Same event as the cabo-verde entity (this benchmark carries Cape Verde as two separate entries): the Fogo Island school-bus crash on 5 September 2026 killed at least 25 people, mostly children, and the government declared national mourning. top_entities.name: Jamaica
top_entities.news_summary: Re-verified carried lead: the Jamaican government signed contracts worth J$1.05 billion (approximately US$6.6 million -- the source specifies the JMD denomination, not USD) on 3 September 2026 for 268 semi-permanent housing units (143 in Westmoreland via DT Brown Construction, 125 in St Elizabeth via Southland Construction) for families displaced by Hurricane Melissa, financed through the National Housing Trust's Shelter Recovery Programme. Positive, moderate, dated humanitarian/governance response; the prior cycle's approximate US$6.3M estimate is consistent with this re-verified US$6.6M figure (both derive from the same J$1.05bn base at differing JMD/USD rates).

top_entities.name: Liechtenstein
top_entities.news_summary: Liechtenstein's parliament voted 13-12 on 7 September 2026 to permit abortion in the first 12 weeks of pregnancy, originating from a popular initiative that gathered signatures from roughly a quarter of the electorate; Hereditary Prince Alois has indicated he will veto the measure, and parliament separately rejected a public referendum on the question. On 8 September, unknown actors breached Liechtenstein's beneficial-ownership registry (VwbP), copying data on roughly 31,000 legal entities.

top_entities.name: Uruguay
top_entities.news_summary: Uruguay is developing a 'democratic' anti-crime strategy explicitly positioned as an alternative to El Salvador-style militarized security policy, aiming to reduce homicides without adopting Bukele-style mass-detention measures, amid rising domestic concern about crime in a country still ranked among Latin America's safest. Positive governance signal on a rights-respecting approach to public safety.

top_entities.name: Portugal
top_entities.news_summary: Portugal secured a EUR1.5 billion European Investment Bank loan (announced 7 September 2026) to finance construction/renovation of roughly 50,000 social housing units. Separately, the European Commission's new 'housing pressure' status, applicable to Portugal, was reported 14 September; over half of Portuguese municipalities meet the EU's criteria for housing-stress designation. Positive governance response to an acute affordability crisis (Portugal recorded the strongest real house-price rise among 57 BIS-tracked economies in Q1 2026).

top_entities.name: Hong Kong
top_entities.news_summary: Three leaders of the Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China (which organized the city's Tiananmen vigil for three decades) -- including human-rights lawyer Chow Hang-tung (sentenced 7y3mo), former lawmaker Lee Cheuk-yan (7y) and Albert Ho (5y2mo, pleaded guilty) -- were sentenced to prison on 11 September 2026 on national-security charges of inciting subversion, after being held in custody for years since 2021 charges.

top_entities.name: Mozambique
top_entities.news_summary: Islamic State Mozambique (ISM) attacked a tourist hunting camp in the Marangira Hunting Area of Niassa Special Reserve on 3 September 2026 -- the group's first incursion into Niassa province since May 2025 -- killing at least one person, displacing roughly 2,700 people, abducting up to 20 workers (including a South African) and destroying tourism infrastructure; several Americans were evacuated by 4 September.

top_entities.name: Poland
top_entities.news_summary: Registered Ukrainian refugees in Poland fell from 974,500 (April 2026) to 868,000 by early September 2026 (an 11% decline), driven substantially by a legal change that removed Ukrainians from the temporary-protection registry over documentation issues, compounded by hardening public attitudes (support for accepting refugees fell from 94% in 2022 to 42% by July 2026).

top_entities.name: South Korea
top_entities.news_summary: South Korea's Financial Industry Union (representing ~100,000 workers) staged a strike (announced 3 September, held 4 September 2026) opposing the government's plan to relocate public financial institutions out of Seoul. Separately, a disability-rights group ended nearly five years of rush-hour subway protests in mid-September after Seoul Metropolitan Council's Democratic Party members pledged ordinances guaranteeing mobility and employment rights for people with disabilities -- a positive resolution.

top_entities.name: Spain
top_entities.news_summary: Tens of thousands protested across Spain (Madrid ~50,000, plus Barcelona, Valencia and Seville) on 2 September 2026 over the government's handling of the Ceuta migration crisis, blaming PM Pedro Sanchez; clashes with police involved plastic bullets and tear gas in Madrid. Note: the underlying mass border crossing and death toll (approximately 80-100 dead) occurred on 30-31 July 2026 -- outside this scan's window -- so this record is flagged on the September protest response, not on new July deaths.

top_entities.name: Boeing
top_entities.news_summary: Boeing's payment of a US$3.1 million FAA fine over widespread 737-factory and Spirit AeroSystems quality-system violations (tied to the 2024 Alaska Airlines MAX 9 door-plug blowout) -- paid quietly in January 2026 -- was publicly disclosed for the first time on 2 September 2026 when the FAA confirmed the payment to Reuters. Carried forward from the prior cycle and re-verified: the fine amount, payment date (January 2026) and disclosure date (2 September 2026) are independently confirmed across multiple dated outlets.

top_entities.name: Los Angeles
top_entities.news_summary: The House Oversight Subcommittee (DOGE) escalated its investigation into the Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority (LAHSA), which has received over $1 billion in federal funding since 2021; Chairman Tim Burchett formally summoned Mayor Karen Bass to testify on 15 September 2026 (letter dated 2 September) over alleged 'wanton mismanagement of public funds.' As of 7 September, Bass indicated she was 'not available' to testify but would provide requested documents dating to 2020. Carried forward from the prior cycle and re-verified with updated developments (summons letter, Bass's non-appearance).

top_entities.name: Indonesia
top_entities.news_summary: Political fallout from Indonesia's late-August riots (which began 25 August over legislator pay hikes and escalated after police killed a motorcycle-taxi driver on 28 August, leaving at least 10 dead and 20 missing) continued into September, with a 2 September Foreign Policy analysis describing President Prabowo Subianto as 'circled by rivals amid Jakarta riots.' Note: the casualty figures (10 dead, 20 missing) date to the 25-28 August unrest, outside this scan's window; the September evidence is the continuing political crisis, not new deaths.

sector_alerts.summary: At least 26 people had reportedly died in ICE custody in 2026 as of 1 September, on pace to exceed 2025's record 33 deaths (the highest in over two decades). HRW's June 2026 report and ongoing reporting cite overcrowding and inadequate medical care. Cross-cutting context for Fortune-500 private-detention operators (CoreCivic, GEO Group) rather than a single-entity flag this cycle -- no dated September-specific death was identified tied to a named facility operator.

sector_alerts.theme: Iran-Gulf regional war escalation (late discovery -- flagged for next-cycle priority)
sector_alerts.summary: A global-cities batch sweep on Baku/Beirut/Kuwait City/Riyadh surfaced evidence of an active, months-long Iran war (day 198 as of 13 September 2026) with direct Iranian strikes reported on Riyadh, Kuwait City (fuel depot fire, intercepted drones) and Beirut, and US-Iran exchanges affecting Hormuz shipping. This was discovered late in this cycle via a broad city sweep, not via dedicated individual searches on Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, or Iran as country entities, and was not independently re-verified against each affected country's own benchmark record this cycle. Disclosed as a coverage gap: Gulf-state and Iran country entities should receive dedicated Tier-1-equivalent attention next cycle given the apparent scale of this conflict.

sector_alerts.theme: DR Congo Ebola status -- not a benchmarked entity
sector_alerts.summary: The carried-lead note about DR Congo's Ebola outbreak status (and the confirmed prior misattribution of Uganda's 'outbreak over' declaration to DRC) could not be re-verified against a DRC entity record because the Democratic Republic of Congo is NOT present in this benchmark's countries index (only 'Republic of Congo' / Congo-Brazzaville is present, consistent with CLAUDE.md's note that 14 of 207 countries are absent from the source data). No entity-level action is possible; recorded here for the founder's awareness only.

A T2 batch search surfaced a 'Miami homeless attack, two dead' story without a clear year. Dedicated verification confirmed the attack (Brenton Clarke charged with killing two homeless people with a stick in downtown Miami) occurred in January 2025, not September 2026. DROPPED from all entity flags per evidence-date discipline -- this is exactly the class of undated/misdated-snippet error the gate is designed to catch.

sector_alerts.theme: Dropped candidate: Lesotho AGOA extension (wrong date AND wrong substance)
sector_alerts.summary: A batch search surfaced a claim that 'AGOA extended to 31 Dec 2028, effective 2 September 2026' for Lesotho. Dedicated verification (per the carried-lead re-verification discipline) found this both misdated and substantively wrong: the actual AGOA reauthorization was signed into law on 3 February 2026 and extends the programme only through 31 December 2026 (the House-passed three-year extension to 2028 did not become law). DROPPED entirely rather than patched with a better source, since the underlying substance -- not just the date -- was incorrect.

sector_alerts.theme: AI Safety Index (Summer 2026) -- three frontier labs graded failing
sector_alerts.summary: The Future of Life Institute's Summer 2026 AI Safety Index gives Anthropic the top overall grade; xAI, DeepSeek and Mistral AI each receive a failing grade in at least one domain (Mistral scored last on safety among all graded labs). Also flagged: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind and Meta -- which previously barred military applications -- have gradually reversed that policy between 2024 and 2026, joining xAI and Mistral in pursuing military use cases. Cross-cutting ai-labs sector context; not a single dated September event.

sector_alerts.theme: EU AI Act shifts to active enforcement
sector_alerts.summary: September 2026 marks a shift from preliminary EU AI Act administrative preparation to active statutory enforcement: the European AI Office and national data-protection authorities began technical audits of Article 11 files for high-risk systems deployed after 2 August 2026. Separately, the EU's Digital Omnibus (7 May 2026) deferred the Annex III high-risk compliance deadline from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027. Cross-cutting ai-labs sector context.

sector_alerts.theme: UK: 40 child asylum seekers went missing (1 September -- one day outside window)
sector_alerts.summary: Reporting that 40 child asylum seekers went missing from UK asylum hotels dates to 1 September 2026 -- one day before this cycle's 2 September window start. Not used to drive a UK entity flag per the evidence-date discipline rule that evidence must fall inside the declared lookback window; noted here as a near-miss the next cycle should pick up if it recurs or is still unresolved.

sector_alerts.theme: Iran: Qarchak prison deaths -- single-source, not independently corroborated
sector_alerts.summary: NCRI (National Council of Resistance of Iran, an Iranian opposition group) reported three women died in Qarchak prison in September 2026 from denied medical care. Carried in entity_reviews as evidence_found with an explicit single-source caution and deliberately excluded from top_entities pending independent corroboration (UN, HRW, wire service) in a future cycle.

sector_alerts.theme: Nepal death toll revised upward repeatedly within one week
sector_alerts.summary: The Nepal flood death toll has been revised upward three times across this and the prior (quarantined) cycle: 1,050 (1 Sept, Al Jazeera), 1,114 (2 Sept, NDRRMA, carried lead), 1,356 (7 Sept, NDRRMA) and 1,386 (12 Sept, NDRRMA, used in this scan). Disclosed explicitly because rapidly-revised death tolls are exactly the kind of figure the evidence-date discipline requires re-verifying rather than assuming static -- the assessor should use the 1,386 figure (12 September) and check for further revision before publishing.
